name: sticky-scroll-reveal
title: Sticky Scroll Reveal
description: A scroll-driven feature section: paragraphs sit on the left while a sticky gradient tile on the right shows the matching visual. As you scroll, the active paragraph brightens and both the tile and the panel background change colour.
use: A feature walkthrough where each paragraph needs its own visual and a change of mood while scrolling.
avoid: Fewer than four items: the fixed-height inner scroll leaves awkward empty space.
a11y: No list semantics or aria; inactive text sits at 30% opacity and the inner scroll area is not keyboard focusable. (keyboard: partial, labels: none, reduced motion: not handled)
looks: A dark panel split in two: a left column of bold white headings and small grey paragraphs, and a rounded square gradient tile on the right holding a centred label. The panel background is deep navy or near-black, and the tile shifts between green, purple and orange gradients.
behaves: Scrolling the inner panel moves the text column past a sticky tile. The item nearest the top fades up to full opacity while the others dim, and the tile gradient plus the panel background switch to the next colour.
customise: Pass a content array of title, description and an optional visual node; colours, gradients and the inner panel height are fixed in the source.
weight: light: Text plus one sticky tile; work happens only while scrolling.
demo: Four items: Collaborative Editing, Real time changes, Version control, Running out of content.
issues: Inactive paragraphs render at 30% opacity on dark, hard to read.
The gradient tile is hidden below the lg breakpoint.
Later frames crop the top text mid-line.
polishWhy: Clean two-column rhythm and a smooth colour shift; faded inactive copy is hard to read.
